content: Healthcare facilities are established to comprehensively address water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) needs. Research is conducted to gather detailed data on the current situation and to identify the most effective interventions tailored to the local context. Monitoring systems are in place to ensure regular and systematic evaluation of all WASH dimensions. These systems utilize surveillance checklists to measure the availability and functionality of services. Monitoring aligns with international indicators and definitions, such as those from WHO, UNICEF, and SDG 6. Data collected through these systems are used to develop, review, and implement national policies and targets. A national overview of WASH in healthcare facilities is available. Specific financial plans or budget lines for WASH are established, and expenditures and needs are systematically monitored to inform planning. A national overview of annual WASH expenditures in healthcare facilities, including segregated data for urban and rural areas, is available. Funding allocation aligns with government priorities and is sufficient to meet local needs. Donor investments and projects are coordinated at the national level. National health strategic plans and policies define quality and WASH according to the local context. Quality is explicitly referenced in national planning documents and is a national priority. Current or proposed initiatives to improve quality are identified, along with specific budgetary provisions for quality-related activities. Regulatory and legislative requirements for healthcare quality and safety, such as licensing, external evaluations, and accreditation, are in place. National surveillance is regulated, with measures and indicators for quality of care, including WASH, infection prevention and control (IPC), and patient safety. National health information policies prioritize quality, incorporating WASH indicators into health information systems and ensuring public access to health service performance data. Strategies, standards, and guidelines for WASH in healthcare facilities, IPC, and patient safety are aligned with national quality improvement efforts. Essential health service packages include criteria related to quality and WASH. Emergency preparedness plans ensure the maintenance of quality healthcare delivery during conflicts, disasters, or public health emergencies, including COVID-19 preparedness and recovery plans that emphasize hand hygiene access for all. Patient rights charters include quality considerations, and standards of care are aligned with national quality policies. The private sector's involvement in WASH service delivery is regulated, with business models and quality standards enforced. National surveys and surveillance data provide insights into WASH service coverage, IPC practices, and maternal and child health outcomes. At the sub-national level, health strategies and plans include quality and WASH services, aligning with national directions. Community and patient engagement in planning and execution of quality health services is emphasized. Health system decentralization allows regions, districts, and communities autonomy in managing health service delivery, with mechanisms in place to coordinate efforts between national and district levels. At the facility level, quality improvement strategies for WASH, IPC, and patient safety are implemented, with funding allocated for these efforts. Mechanisms for learning and feedback are established to support continuous improvement. Facilities are equipped with handwashing stations, sufficient toilets, and reliable electricity. Data collection and reporting systems are used to assess quality of care and inform decision-making. Staff are trained in quality, IPC, and WASH, and patient feedback systems are in place to address complaints and improve services. Research and evidence are routinely used to guide clinical care, and facilities participate in research initiatives. Decision-making processes for budget allocation are transparent, and gaps in resources are identified and addressed. Staff are supported with training and resources to deliver quality care, fostering a culture of change and improvement at all levels.
